title: Install Windows updates & drivers
description: Run Windows Update to install the latest OS updates. This MUST be done right after logging in, before anything else.
helpText:
Do NOT move this later in the guide. It must happen immediately after successfully logging into Windows.

1. Open Settings → Windows Update (ms-settings:windowsupdate).
2. Click Check for updates.
3. Install ALL available Windows updates.
4. Restart the computer if requested.
5. After restarting, check Windows Update AGAIN.
6. Continue checking until there are no important pending Windows updates.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Windows Update screen]

Click Mark Completed once no important updates remain.

title: Dell driver / BIOS update (if Dell laptop)
description: Conditional — only if the laptop is a Dell. Use Dell SupportAssist for driver/BIOS/firmware updates, then re-check Windows Update.
helpText:
CONDITIONAL STEP — only applies IF the laptop is a Dell. If it is not a Dell, skip this step and mark it complete.

1. Open Dell Support (click 'Open Link' to go there).
2. Search for: Dell SupportAssist
3. Download and install Dell SupportAssist.
4. Open SupportAssist.
5. Perform a Full System Scan.
6. Install available driver, BIOS, and recommended system updates.
7. Allow the laptop to restart when required.

IMPORTANT — after SupportAssist finishes and the laptop restarts:
Go back to Settings → Windows Update, check for updates again, install any remaining updates, and restart if required.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Dell SupportAssist]

Click Mark Completed once driver/BIOS updates are finished.

title: Test GlobalProtect VPN
description: Only after Windows and driver updates are complete, test the GlobalProtect VPN connection.
helpText:
Only after Windows and driver updates are complete should you test the VPN.

1. Open GlobalProtect.
2. Try to connect.
3. Wait for the connection to establish.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — GlobalProtect connection]

IF GlobalProtect CONNECTS SUCCESSFULLY:
Do NOT troubleshoot it further. Mark this step complete and continue to the next phase.

The user can now proceed with the normal company-access setup.

IF GlobalProtect does NOT connect:
You may need to request an E5 license before the VPN will work.

Request E5 license:
https://apps.powerapps.com/play/e/a5d82b60-279b-ec72-8a4c-653aa596b309/a/b0c62f94-48f3-4fff-bacb-423952b88389?tenantId=9a309606-d6ec-4188-a28a-298812b4bbbf&hint=54664dd5-1605-4544-91a4-d27b1611c2ce&sourcetime=1759235157351

Click the link above or copy it into your browser to request the E5 license.

While waiting for E5 approval, you can also use the Prisma Browser workaround (see the next step).

title: Diagnose the GlobalProtect error (conditional)
description: Conditional — only if GlobalProtect failed to connect. Identify the error so you take the correct path.
helpText:
CONDITIONAL STEP — only follow this if GlobalProtect did NOT connect. If it connected, skip this whole branch and continue the main flow.

When GlobalProtect fails, check the error message. Examples:
- Authentication Failed
- Authorization / access problem
- License-related problem
- Unable to connect
- Other VPN error

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — GlobalProtect error]

If the error is an authentication or authorization problem, the required next action depends on your employee type:
- Fixed Employee → follow normal IT troubleshooting / access procedure.
- Contractor → the required E5 license may be missing; see the 'Request E5 license' step.

Click Mark Completed once you have identified the error and your path.

title: Request E5 license (contractors only)
description: Conditional — contractors may need to request an E5 license before GlobalProtect works. Not needed for fixed employees.
helpText:
For contractors, GlobalProtect may require an E5 license. If you received an authentication/authorization problem because the required E5 license is missing, raise the appropriate IT request for the E5 license.

The request portal is: apps.powerapps.com (open the access request portal).

Explain in the request:
- Where/what application/service to search for.
- What information needs to be provided (SSO number, reason).
- What to do after submitting the request (wait for approval before VPN-dependent steps).

1. Click Request Upgrade.
2. Select your GE HealthCare account.
3. Choose: New GEHC PC or MAC.
4. Reason: Requesting the Microsoft E5 license upgrade to enable GlobalProtect VPN access and support engineering development on my workstation.
5. Submit the request and wait for approval before continuing VPN-dependent steps.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — E5 license request]

[IMAGE / INSTRUCTION PLACEHOLDER — Exact E5 license request procedure]

title: Install Prisma Browser (temporary workaround)
description: Conditional — use Prisma Browser as a temporary workaround while waiting for GlobalProtect/E5/access to become available.
helpText:
While waiting for the E5 license / GlobalProtect access, you can install and use Prisma Browser as a temporary workaround.

Use the official guide:
https://pulse.service-now.com/mth?id=kb_article&sysparm_article=KB00308598

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Prisma Browser installation/setup]

After Prisma Browser is available, use it to access GE Healthcare applications where required.

Return to the main flow once GlobalProtect / E5 access becomes available.

title: Request application access via MyAccess (conditional)
description: Conditional — if a specific application is unavailable or access is denied, request access through MyAccess. Separate from VPN setup.
helpText:
APPLICATION ACCESS is separate from VPN access. Do NOT mix application-specific access requests into VPN troubleshooting.

If VPN/Prisma Browser is working but a particular application is unavailable or access is denied, request the required access through MyAccess.

Example — Box Access:
1. Go to http://myaccess.gehealthcare.com
2. Click Start an Access Request.
3. Select Application.
4. Search for BOX.
5. Click Add.
6. Click Next.
7. Review the request.
8. Click Submit.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Box MyAccess request]

Example — Confluence Access:
Try https://ge-hc.atlassian.net/wiki/home
If access is unavailable:
1. Open https://edh.apps.ge-healthcare.net/confluence/
2. Select Account Creation / Reactivation.
3. Search for Confluence Global SaaS.
4. Complete the request.
5. Submit the request. (No attachment required.)

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Confluence access request]

Click Mark Completed once your required application access is requested.

title: Bookmark important company resources
description: Bookmark Box, Confluence, CoreData, Emerge U / Learner Dashboard, MyAccess, and GitLab once the network/VPN is usable.
helpText:
Once the network/VPN situation is sufficiently usable, bookmark the important company resources.

The preferred browser can be Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, or another approved browser.

Recommended bookmarks:
- Box — cloud storage and file sharing.
- Confluence — internal documentation and knowledge base. Try https://ge-hc.atlassian.net/wiki/home
- CoreData — attendance / time management.
- Learner Dashboard / Emerge U — training and onboarding courses.
- MyAccess — requests for applications, licenses, permissions, etc.
- GitLab — repository https://gitlab.apps.ge-healthcare.net/WomensHealthUltrasound/SystemSource.git
  (preserve the GitLab base URL https://gitlab.apps.ge)

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Recommended browser bookmarks]

Run the bookmark script or add them manually.

Click Mark Completed once the bookmarks are in place.

title: Complete GenAI training (Emerge U)
description: Complete the required 'Use of GenAI for Software Development' course on Emerge U and obtain the completion certificate.
helpText:
Before beginning project development, complete the required onboarding/compliance training. Training is also useful while waiting for VPN, E5, GitLab, Copilot, or license access.

To obtain access for APP_Gitlab, SCIM_gehc_ghemu-copilot, and SCIM_gehc_ghemuall, complete the required Emerge U learning course.

1. In Emerge U / Learner Dashboard, search for: Use of GenAI for Software Development
2. Open the course/video.
3. Watch the approximately 55m 48s training video.
4. Complete the course.
5. Obtain the completion certificate/diploma.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Emerge U course search]
[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Course completion certificate]

Click Mark Completed once the course and certificate are done.

title: Email manager about GenAI access approval
description: After GenAI training, email your manager requesting approval for GitHub Copilot / GitLab access, and wait for the approval reply.
helpText:
Step 1 — After completing the GenAI training, take a screenshot showing the completed training/certificate.

Step 2 — Email the manager requesting approval for the required GitHub Copilot/GitLab access. Use this template:

"Hallo Mr.[Manager Name],

According to the provided guide, I require your approval via email in order to proceed with my access request and license for GitHub Copilot.

Could you please confirm your approval in this Email so that I can continue with the request process?

Thank you in advance for your support.

Best regards,
[Your Name]"

Step 3 — Wait for the manager's approval response.

Step 4 — After receiving the approval, take a screenshot containing the relevant email conversation showing the request and the manager's approval.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Email approval conversation]

Click Mark Completed once the manager has approved.

title: Request GitLab / Copilot access in Saviynt
description: Submit the GitLab, Copilot, and standard access requests in Saviynt (Prod - Ping Directory), attaching the manager approval and certificate.
helpText:
After the manager approves, submit the access requests in Saviynt.

1. Open https://gehealthcare.saviyntcloud.com/ECMv6/request/requestHome
2. Search for: ping
3. Select: Prod - Ping Directory
4. Click: Next

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Saviynt search for Ping]

5. Select ALL required access items:
   - APP_Gitlab
   - SCIM_gehc_ghemu-copilot
   - SCIM_gehc_ghemuall
6. Click: Next

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Select GitLab/Copilot access]

7. Attach documentation:
   - Screenshot of the manager approval email/conversation.
   - Training completion certificate.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Attach approval and certificate]

8. Check: 'I confirm that I have reviewed this request and that I need this access to do my job.'
9. Click: Submit

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Confirmation checkbox and Submit]

Click Mark Completed once the requests are submitted.

title: Install preferred browser (optional)
description: Optional — install Google Chrome or another approved browser and bookmark the frequently used company resources.
helpText:
OPTIONAL — install Chrome or another approved browser if required. This is a convenience step and must NOT block development setup.

1. If using Chrome, run the installer (it skips installation if Chrome is already present).
2. Bookmark frequently used company resources.

Common bookmarks include:
- CoreData
- Pulse
- Emerge U / Learner Dashboard
- Other frequently used company resources

The installer skips installation if Chrome is already present.

Click Mark Completed once the browser is ready.

title: Prepare the disk (shrink C:, create D:)
description: Create a dedicated data partition (for example D:) for engineering source and build artifacts.
helpText:
After the basic Windows/network/access setup is underway, prepare the development machine disk.

Open Windows Search and search for: Create and format hard disk partitions
Open: Create and format hard disk partitions

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Disk Management]

1. Shrink the C: drive:
   - Right-click the C: volume.
   - Select Shrink Volume.
   - Try to create an approximately 50/50 split between C: and the new D: volume.
   - Complete the shrink operation.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Shrink Volume]

2. Create the D: volume:
   - After shrinking, an Unallocated area will appear.
   - Right-click the Unallocated space.
   - Select New Simple Volume.
   - Choose drive letter: D:
   - Click Next, Next, Next, Next, Finish.
   - No special changes are required unless team documentation says otherwise.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — New Simple Volume]

3. IF required by the team's development setup, create the folder D:\ARCHIVE.
   This is TEAM/SETUP DEPENDENT and NOT mandatory.

Close Disk Management.

Click Mark Completed once the D: partition exists.

title: Create C:\dev\master workspace
description: Create the C:\dev\master folder that hosts the cloned repository.
helpText:
1. Open the C: drive.
2. Create the folder C:\dev.
3. Inside it create C:\dev\master.

The final directory must be: C:\dev\master

This is where the SystemSource repository will be cloned.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — C:\dev\master]

Click Mark Completed once the folder exists.

title: Install Visual Studio
description: Install Visual Studio (2022 Professional or the currently required team version) and import the team's VS configuration file.
helpText:
Install Visual Studio 2022 Professional OR the currently required team Visual Studio version.

[VERIFY — Confirm the current required Visual Studio edition/version for this team.]

Import the team's configuration file: VS_2026_Configuration.vsconfig

The existing team configuration also references a Visual Studio configuration file (Configs\vs2026.vsconfig and Configs\VS2022.vsconfig). Do not remove this information.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Visual Studio installer]
[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Import VS configuration]

Run the installer with the team VS config, then click Mark Completed.

title: Install .NET SDK
description: Install the required .NET SDK used for building the solution.
helpText:
Install the .NET SDK.

The required version is the .NET 10.0.100 SDK.

Download and install it while the repository is cloning to save time.

The install script uses: Configs\Installers\dotnet-sdk-10.0.301-win-x64.exe

Note: some documentation also references dotnet-sdk-10.0.109-win-x64.exe. The 10.0.100 SDK is the confirmed required baseline; use the version the project/tooling actually needs.

Run the installer on this desktop, then click Mark Completed.

title: Install Windows SDK
description: Install the Windows SDK required for Win32 and driver development.
helpText:
If using the current Visual Studio setup, install the required Windows SDK.

Installer file: Configs\Installers\winsdksetup.exe

Run the installer to add the Windows SDK, then click Mark Completed.

title: Install Git & Git Bash
description: Install Git and the Git Bash shell for version control workflows.
helpText:
Install Git, Git Extensions, and Git Bash following the team's existing Git configuration documentation.

If the team documentation says to skip SSH configuration, explicitly state: Skip the SSH configuration section and continue with the relevant team setup instructions.

Do not invent authentication methods.

Run the installer. Git is required for cloning and daily source control.

Click Mark Completed when the script finishes.

title: Install Git Extensions
description: Install the GitExtensions graphical Git client used for repository management.
helpText:
Run the installer to add Git Extensions for visual repository interaction.

Click Mark Completed when the script finishes.

title: Create GitLab access token
description: Generate and securely save a GitLab personal access token required to clone and interact with the SystemSource repository.
helpText:
Create the required GitLab access token.

1. Click 'Open Link' to open GitLab.
2. Generate a personal access token with read_repository / write_repository scope.

IMPORTANT:
- Copy the token immediately and store it somewhere safe.
- The token will be required when cloning the repository.
- Do NOT expose or display the token in screenshots.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Create GitLab access token]

Click Mark Completed once the token is safely stored.

title: Configure Git / Git Extensions
description: Configure Git and Git Extensions according to the team documentation BEFORE cloning the repository.
helpText:
Configure Git and Git Extensions according to the existing team documentation. This must happen BEFORE cloning the repository.

[VERIFY — Confirm the exact Git/Git Extensions configuration values with the team documentation.]

- Set the Git user name and email as required by the team.
- Apply the team's Git Extensions settings.

If the team documentation says to skip SSH configuration, skip it and continue.

Reference: Wili Doc (team procedure).

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Git Extensions configuration]

Click Mark Completed once Git is configured.

title: Configure getBinaries / Voluson scripts
description: Configure getBinaries and the Voluson configuration tool scripts as required by the team instructions.
helpText:
Open Git Extensions as required by the existing team instructions.

Configure:
- getBinaries
- Voluson configuration tool scripts

Reference: Wili Doc (team procedure). Keep this reference because it is part of the existing team procedure.

[VERIFY — Confirm the exact getBinaries / Voluson script configuration with the team documentation.]

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — getBinaries / Voluson script configuration]

Click Mark Completed once the scripts are configured.

title: Add Git usr\bin to Windows PATH
description: Add C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin to the Windows PATH environment variable.
helpText:
1. Open Environment Variables.
2. Locate the Path variable.
3. Click Edit / New.
4. Enter: C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin
5. Confirm the changes (OK / Apply).

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Environment Variables / PATH]

Click Mark Completed once the PATH is updated.

title: Clone the SystemSource repository
description: Clone the WomensHealthUltrasound SystemSource repository into C:\dev\master using your GitLab access token.
helpText:
CLONING MUST COME AFTER Git configuration. Now clone the project.

Repository: https://gitlab.apps.ge-healthcare.net/WomensHealthUltrasound/SystemSource.git
Destination: C:\dev\master

Click 'Open Link' to open the repository in your browser, then clone it to the destination.

Authentication — when prompted:
- Username: your SSO number (example: 123456789)
- Password: the GitLab access token created earlier

Do NOT use the normal GE email address as the Git username unless the team's current GitLab configuration specifically requires it.

NETWORK — the repository may be large. Cloning may take up to approximately 30 minutes. Connect the laptop to Ethernet if available for the fastest, most reliable transfer.

PARALLEL — while the repository is cloning, continue with independent setup tasks such as SDK installation (they do not depend on the repository being downloaded).

Verify the clone succeeded before continuing.

Click Mark Completed once the clone finishes.

title: Apply Archive registry configuration
description: Apply the Archive registry configuration from the cloned repository.
helpText:
Only after the repository has successfully finished cloning should you continue with repository-specific configuration.

1. Verify the repository exists at C:\dev\master and the expected project structure is present.
2. The main project location should be: C:\dev\master\V730

Then:
1. Go to C:\dev\master\V730\Distribution\RegFiles
2. Find: Archive
3. Double-click it.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Archive file]

Click Mark Completed.

title: Run SetSerialNr
description: Run the SetSerialNr registry file from the cloned repository.
helpText:
1. Go to C:\dev\master\V730\Distribution\RegFiles\ForDebug
2. Find: SetSerialNr
3. Double-click it.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — SetSerialNr]

Click Mark Completed once the serial number is applied.

title: Configure VolusonConfigTool
description: Start and configure VolusonConfigTool with the team's required settings.
helpText:
1. Go to C:\dev\master\Binaries\Debug\bin
2. Start: VolusonConfigTool
3. Configure it according to the team's required settings.

The exact configuration should be demonstrated using the screenshot that will be added later.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — VolusonConfigTool configuration]

[VERIFY — Confirm the exact VolusonConfigTool settings with the team. Do not invent configuration values; the screenshot will be the source of truth.]

Click Mark Completed once configured.

title: Install required fonts (SourceSansProWHUS)
description: Install the six SourceSansProWHUS TrueType fonts from the cloned repository.
helpText:
1. Go to C:\dev\master\V730\Distribution\Data\Fonts\SourceSansProWHUS
2. There should be 6 TrueType font files.
3. Run/install all six font files.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — SourceSansProWHUS fonts]

Click Mark Completed once the fonts are installed.

title: Run getBinaries
description: Run the getBinaries step to retrieve any required third-party binaries for the build.
helpText:
1. Go to C:\dev\master
2. Run: getBinaries.bat

If the procedure requires running the getBinaries batch script separately, execute it according to the team's documentation.

[VERIFY — Confirm the exact getBinaries execution order with the team documentation.]

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — getBinaries.bat]

Click Mark Completed once getBinaries succeeds.

title: Open & build Voluson.sln
description: Open the Voluson solution in Visual Studio and build it successfully, then run the project.
helpText:
Once all configuration and dependencies are complete:

1. Open Visual Studio.
2. Select Open a project or solution.
3. Navigate to C:\dev\master\V730 and open Voluson.sln.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Open Voluson.sln]

4. Allow Visual Studio to finish loading the solution.
5. Restore/build any required dependencies.
6. Build the solution (Build > Rebuild Solution).
7. Resolve any expected first-run setup issues using the troubleshooting / verification section.
8. Run the application.

[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Build Solution]
[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Run project]

Click Mark Completed once the build and run succeed.

title: Final verification & onboarding checklist
description: Confirm the whole environment and run the Validation section, then complete the final onboarding checklist.
helpText:
The onboarding process is complete ONLY when the user can:

- Log into Windows.
- Install all required Windows updates.
- Install required hardware/driver/BIOS updates.
- Successfully connect to GlobalProtect OR use the approved temporary Prisma Browser path while waiting for required access.
- Access required company resources.
- Complete required onboarding training.
- Request/obtain required GitLab/Copilot access.
- Install Visual Studio.
- Install/configure required SDKs.
- Install and configure Git.
- Create the development directory.
- Clone SystemSource successfully.
- Complete repository configuration.
- Configure VolusonConfigTool.
- Install the required fonts.
- Run the binary retrieval process (getBinaries).
- Open Voluson.sln.
- Build the project.
- Run the project successfully.

Final step — run the Validation section (Validation page → Run Validation), review the results, and resolve any ERROR items.

TROUBLESHOOTING — use a clear structure: Problem → Cause/Condition → Action → Return to Main Flow.
Example: GlobalProtect Authentication Failed → check contractor/E5 → request E5 → install Prisma Browser while waiting → continue with onboarding → return to normal flow when VPN access is available.

Click Mark Completed once validation is clean.

title: Initial Windows laptop setup
description: Finish the out-of-the-box Windows setup: region, keyboard, Wi-Fi, and sign in with your SSO number (not your email).
helpText:
The very first thing after receiving the laptop is the normal Windows setup.

1. Choose Country or Region.
2. Choose Keyboard Layout.
3. Connect to the company Wi-Fi:
   - Network: INTERNET
   - Password: Acc3ssGr@nted
4. Log in using the company credentials.

IMPORTANT — username is the SSO number, NOT the email address.

Example SSO: 123456789
Example email (do NOT use): 123456789@gehealthcare.com

The actual login identifier is: 123456789

Password requirements:
- At least 15 characters.

Click Mark Completed once you are signed in to Windows.

title: Complete SSO & device enrollment
description: Finish single sign-on and Microsoft InTune device enrollment so the workstation is fully managed.
helpText:
1. Open the Company Portal / InTune app.
2. Sign in and complete device enrollment.
3. Confirm the device shows as compliant.

Click Mark Completed once enrollment is finished.
